LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 7.1.1: LISTENING FOR DETAIL

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 7
Topic 7.1: Listening and Speaking 7.1.1: Listening for Detail
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 7.1.1: Listening for Detail, part of Strand 7 in Grade 8 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: How should one listen for detail?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. listen to a recorded text on wild life and answer questions from the text, and discuss the main ideas,

2. listen to a passage read by peers or the teacher and outline the main ideas from the text individually,

3. discuss with peers answers based on a given text.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. listen to a recorded text on wild life and answer questions from the text, and discuss the main ideas,
2. listen to a passage read by peers or the teacher and outline the main ideas from the text individually,
3. discuss with peers answers based on a given text.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 7.1.1: Listening for Detail together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication: It is promoted as the learner listens keenly and actively and responds to questions.

• Digital literacy: It is enhanced as the learner interacts with digital devices when listening to a recorded text.

Values:
• Patriotism: It is promoted as the learner nurtures the love of their country by interacting with texts on Kenya’s rich wildlife

heritage.

• Responsibility: It is promoted as the learner is sensitised on the importance of wildlife.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Wildlife conservation: It is enhanced as the learner interacts with information about wildlife.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The leaner develops listening for detail and is able to relate it to their learning in Kiswahili.
